common_name: Rosita Eggplant (Rutgers-Bred Puerto Rican-Type Lavender Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8 weeks before last frost; transplant once nights stay warm. Rosita was bred at Rutgers specifically for growers serving Puerto Rican and Caribbean markets.

directions: Rosita produces blocky, egg-shaped fruit with pale lavender-pink skin and creamy white flesh that stays mild and tender even as fruit sizes up, a trait bred in by Rutgers to suit fresh-market growers serving Caribbean and Latino communities. The vigorous, heat-loving plants set fruit reliably through hot, humid summers and hold up well without staking in most home gardens. Pick fruit while still glossy at 4-6 inches long for the best texture, since the thin skin means it bruises more easily than thicker-skinned purple types. Its milder flavor and lower seed count make it a good choice for cooks who find standard purple-black eggplant too bitter or seedy.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station

common_name: Kamo Eggplant (Kamo Nasu, Kyoto Heirloom Round Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost; give plants extra room since Kamo grows larger and bushier than slender Asian eggplant types.

directions: Kamo Nasu is a traditional heirloom from the Kamo district of Kyoto, grown for its large, softball-sized round fruit with thick, dense flesh that stays creamy and never turns spongy even at full size. It is the classic eggplant used for dengaku, where thick slices are grilled or pan-fried and topped with sweet miso glaze, since the dense flesh holds together better than thinner-skinned slicing types. Give plants rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture, as the large fruit can stress the plant if it dries out between waterings. Choose Kamo when you want an eggplant suited to grilling and roasting whole slices rather than the elongated Asian types more common in home gardens.

common_name: Ghostbuster Eggplant (Glossy White Oval Hybrid Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost; transplant once soil is warm and nights stay above 55°F.

directions: Ghostbuster is a compact, early hybrid eggplant that produces smooth, glossy, pure-white oval fruit with creamy flesh and notably fewer seeds than many heirloom white varieties. Its hybrid vigor and disease resistance make it more forgiving for beginners than older open-pollinated white eggplants, which can be slower and less productive. Harvest fruit at 4-5 inches while the skin is still glossy and firm, since white types can develop a yellow tinge and bitter flavor if left too long on the plant. Choose Ghostbuster when you want the striking look of a white eggplant on a plant with the reliability and earliness of a modern hybrid.

common_name: North and South Okra (Sand Mountain Alabama Heirloom Okra)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed well past last frost; North and South is an Alabama heirloom passed down on Sand Mountain, prized for tender pods produced over a long season.

directions: North and South is a Southern heirloom okra preserved by gardening families on Sand Mountain in northeast Alabama, grown for slim, ridged green pods that stay tender well past the size most okra turns woody. Direct sow after the soil is reliably warm, since okra seedlings are slow to establish in cool soil, and thin plants to give them room to branch. The tall, productive plants keep setting pods over a long summer season if picked every day or two at 3-4 inches. As an open-pollinated heirloom it is easy to save seed from, helping keep a piece of Alabama foodways history in circulation.

planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed well after last frost; Evertender's spineless pods make repeat picking easier through a long harvest season.

directions: Evertender is a spineless hybrid okra bred for pods that stay tender and stringless days longer than most varieties, reducing the pressure to pick every single day to avoid tough, fibrous pods. The smooth, spineless pods and foliage also make harvest far more comfortable, since typical okra plants are covered in fine irritating spines. Direct sow after the soil has warmed, since okra germinates poorly in cool, wet ground, and pick pods at 3-4 inches for the most tender eating. Its extended tenderness window makes Evertender a practical choice for gardeners who can only harvest okra every few days rather than daily.

common_name: Puerto Rico Okra (Tall Tropical Heirloom Okra)

planting.note: Direct sow once soil is warm; give this heirloom extra spacing, since it grows much taller and leafier than most okra varieties.

directions: Puerto Rico okra is a striking tropical heirloom that towers over most garden okra, often reaching 8-12 feet in a long, warm growing season, with correspondingly large leaves and pods that need to be picked young to stay tender. Give it plenty of room and rich soil, since the plant puts substantial energy into its height and canopy before pods come on in quantity. It thrives in the long, hot, humid summers of the Deep South and Gulf Coast, where shorter-season okra varieties can start to slow down in peak heat. Choose it as a dual-purpose plant, since the tall, leafy stand also works as a temporary summer privacy screen or windbreak in the vegetable garden.
